chunks: Samaʿah asked him about his statement: “The fasting person has the option until the sun passes its zenith.” He said:
“That applies to the obligatory fast. As for the voluntary fast, he may break the fast at whatever hour he wishes until sunset.”

key_terms.زَوَالِ: the sun’s passing the zenith, i.e. midday

ai.seo_question: Can a person break a voluntary fast after midday, and does the same rule apply to an obligatory fast?
ai.summary: This hadith distinguishes between obligatory and voluntary fasting regarding the option to discontinue the fast. In obligatory fasting, the limit mentioned is until midday, whereas in a supererogatory fast one may break the fast at any time before sunset.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: Hadith.2002 - Sama‘ah asked Abu ‘Abd Allah (as) about the statement: "The fasting person has the option until the sun passes its zenith."
Imam (as) replied: "That applies to obligatory fasts. As for voluntary fasts, one may break the fast at any time they wish until sunset."
